newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom sees progress on merger benefits.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom sees progress on merger benefits.

text.p: WorldCom Inc's revenue growth remains sustainable at more than 30 percent a year and merger synergies from recent acquisitions are progressing faster than WorldCom had expected, its chief executive said.
"Our plans call for us to be a little bit north of 30 percent," Chief Executive Bernard Ebbers said in a phone interview following WorldCom's second quarter report.

In a conference call slated to begin at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, Ebbers said officials will discuss the strides WorldCom has made acheiving synergies from its merger with local operator MFS Communications Inc and Internet provider UUNET Corp.

In the second quarter, net income before preferred dividends was $79 million, or $0.08 per common share, compared with net income of $100 million, or $0.25 a share in the year ago quarter, before non-recurring charges in the prior period.
WorldCom second quarter earnings were roughly in line with expectations, as revenues grew 33 percent and $0.08 per share was in a penny ahead of Wall Street consensus expectations.

However, the results were not enough to satisfy investors, whom traders had said expected a greater upside surprise. The stock fell 2-1/16 to 33-13/16 in early trading on Thursday and was the most active Nasdaq issue.

WorldCom's total second quarter pro-forma revenues, including the results of acquisitions, were $1.77 billion a 33 percent increase versus $1.33 billion a year ago. Without the acquisitions, its core business grew 65 percent year-to-year.

Second quarter revenues from WorldCom's core domestic phone switching business grew 22 percent to $967 million from $794 million. Domestic private line revenues, which derive from its MFS Communications operations, grew to $372 million from $276 million, an increase of 35 percent.
Second quarter international revenues were $197 million, an 83 percent jump from $108 million in the year ago quarter while Internet revenues leaped 133 percent to $125.8 million.

Speaking of the merger benefits the company is seeing from its recent acquisitions, Ebbers told Reuters that, "I think people will be very pleased with the progress relative to what we had previously said."
Analysts have been projecting such merger benefits to amount to $250 million to $300 million for 1997 as a whole.
A WorldCom spokesman said that second quarter results made the company comfortable it could meet these expectations.

In the interview, Ebbers said the company had made extremely good progress in its European business during the second quarter, due to continuing strong traffic growth in the United Kingdom and a growing presence in Continental Europe.

Ebbers also cited the strong growth in its core domestic long-distance switching business and its local service operations and said he was "extremely excited" at the prospects for its bundled offering of an integrated package of WorldCom's stable of advanced communications services.

He described WorldCom's sales organization as a revenue-production factory and noted that the company's new revenue growth in absolute dollars of $430 million exceeded new revenue growth at its far-larger rivals AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp.

In the statement accompanying the second quarter report, Ebbers said that, "Putting it all together, we are running on all cylinders and, I believe, uniquely positioned for the fundamental changes that are reshaping the marketplace."
But traders said there was little upside earnings surprise to prop up the stock of the fast-growing diversified telecommunications operator.
